title: Leader Election

validation.research: Six primary sources: Microsoft Leader Election guidance, Ongaro and Ousterhout’s Raft paper, official ZooKeeper recipes, etcd concurrency API, Kubernetes Leases documentation, and Kleppmann’s fencing discussion. Leader Election is the established name. Election, consensus, leases, mutexes, and destination fencing are distinguished. Fixed membership, retained one-vote-per-term state, full-group majorities, minority unavailability, liveness assumptions, and safe membership change are explicit. Raft additionally requires log freshness, replication, persistence, and other protocol rules; the example is not Raft. A new election neither kills an old process nor automatically fences an independent resource.

runnable_example.verification: Exact five-line demo output; isolated C cannot win; A wins A/B in term one, competing same-term B fails, and B later wins B/C in term two while A’s immutable historical result survives; newer election alone leaves old A eligible at the independent register until explicit handover; uninstalled newer claims, stale writes, stale installs, and conflicting same-term owners are rejected without mutating the register; duplicate install of current authority preserves value and repeated same-term writes remain eligible, distinguishing fencing from deduplication; lower-term vote rejection and one retained candidate per term; duplicate reachable identities count once; full-membership quorum formula for cohorts 1–7 including even sizes; 384 exhaustive three-member traces cover every candidate order and self-containing reachable subset, with at most one winner per term; split vote stalls until a later successful term; invalid membership, candidate, term, and reachability inputs preserve state; independent model instances do not share voting state. Sequential trusted same-scope model only: no real network, clocks, persistence, safe membership change, process roles, Raft log replication/freshness, authentication, or crash recovery is inferred.

example_limits: Original Python 3.11+ deterministic sequential in-memory simulation. One election scope has 1–7 distinct trusted member identities and positive integer terms. Each voter and register call models an atomic operation. Full-membership majorities and retained one-vote-per-term records prevent different winners within one term under these assumptions. Immutable results are historical observations, not permanent write permission. The independent publication register rejects obsolete writes only after explicit installation of newer authority; election alone does not update it. Production installation must authenticate trusted same-scope authority, and checks plus writes must be atomic with durable monotonic state surviving restore. Same-term writes remain eligible, so fencing does not deduplicate work or establish publication correctness. No real network, process roles, clocks, persistence, Raft log replication/freshness, authentication, safe membership change, crash recovery, or formal protocol verification is inferred. Exhaustive tests cover 384 bounded three-member campaign traces, not all network interleavings.
